newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Amazon society flocks to opera festival.
newsitem.headline: Amazon society flocks to opera festival.

text.p: A glittering Amazon society stepped out in full force on Saturday for the opening night of the first International Opera Festival -- something the city of Manaus had not seen for close to 100 years.
Wearing silk and pearls, the "Manauaras" packed into their beloved Amazon theatre to see the Minsk Bolshoi Orchestra perform Vivaldi's "Four Seasons" and Tchaikovsky's "The Nutcracker Suite."
The highlight of the event was a solo violin performance by Michael Jelden, a 25-year-old German virtuoso.
Jelden conceived the idea of the music festival that will stage three full-scale operas -- "Carmen," "La Traviata" and "The Barber of Seville" -- as well as six concert evenings.
Local newspapers have dubbed Jelden "the new Fitzcarraldo" after the character in Werner Herzog's movie who becomes obsessed with taking opera to the Amazon Indians.

"I did this because it is fun, because it has artistic and human value," said Jelden, who admits he too became obsessed with bringing music to the rainforest after he stumbled across pictures of the Amazon theatre while browsing the Internet.

"It was fantastic," said Amazonino Mendes, governor of the state of Amazonas who admits to not being much of a music lover but who is intent on bringing back a taste of the glories experienced at the height of the rubber boom at the end of the last century.
Rubber barons built the Amazon theatre -- a 640-seat replica of a European opera house. Every steel column, tile and light bulb was imported from Europe and it took 10 years to build.
By then, the rubber boom was mostly over and in 1907 the theatre was forced to close after just 10 opera seasons.

Gov. Amazonino restored the destroyed Amazon theatre to its former glory and last year celebrated its 100th anniversary by spending over $1 million to bring Spanish tenor Jose Carreras to sing in Manaus.
